entries.note: The Metal Shading Language source is a line-for-line port of backend_gl.c's program: mode 0 plain quad, modes 1-3 rounded-box signed distance (fill, ring, shadow), mode 4 coverage atlas, mode 5 RGBA texture, with per-corner radii from the corner mask. Glyph placement, atlas packing, batching and blend factors copy the OpenGL adapter as well, which is why the evidence shows Metal pixel-identical to OpenGL on every scene and therefore inside the same tolerances against the SDL reference. Keep the two shaders and the glyph expressions in step: a change in one adapter changes the comparison numbers for both. The source is compiled at startup with newLibraryWithSource: (spec 072 decision 5) so no Metal toolchain is needed at build time; the vertex layout puts the two float4 attributes first so their offsets are 16-byte aligned (stride 60).

The Metal adapter draws a ramp as one quad per logical pixel, each carrying the whole rectangle's shape parameters. The vertex format already interpolates colour, so a single quad with two colours would have been cheaper, but then this adapter's ramp would be the graphics card's interpolation while the SDL reference stepped it in software, and the comparison in tools/render_compare.py would be measuring the difference between two definitions of a gradient. Stepping every adapter through re_gradient_sample makes the ramp part of the contract instead. Passing the full shape rather than the strip keeps the signed-distance field rounding the ends, so a rounded track needs no special case, and a slider's track costs a couple of hundred quads, which is nothing beside a frame of text.

One command buffer per frame: begin acquires the drawable and opens the encoder, execute ends encoding, and the buffer is committed exactly once. The normal path commits with presentDrawable: from present. The snapshot path commits first (without presenting), waits for completion, reads the drawable's texture back (the layer is created with framebufferOnly = NO for this) and then present only calls present on the drawable, since the buffer is already committed. Presenting a drawable whose buffer has not been committed, or committing twice, is undefined in Metal; the `committed` flag guards both. The layer's drawableSize is set from SDL_Metal_GetDrawableSize every frame so a window resize takes effect before the next nextDrawable. Objective-C objects live in ReMetalObjects behind a __bridge_retained pointer so the C ops table and ReBackend stay plain C; close_backend transfers ownership back so ARC releases them.
